```json
{"rows": [
{"n": 1, "label": "requested", "why": "\"`POST /tickets/import` takes a JSON body {\"tickets\": [...]} whose items are what `POST /tickets` takes ... answers 400 with an error whose message names the first invalid item\""},
{"n": 2, "label": "requested", "why": "\"its requester is notified just as when one ticket is created\""},
{"n": 3, "label": "requested", "why": "\"creates them in the given order: all of them, or none when any item is invalid\""},
{"n": 4, "label": "implied", "why": "The all-or-none, in-order import would interleave with or corrupt other concurrent writes unless store mutation is serialized."},
{"n": 5, "label": "requested", "why": "\"at most 5000 of them\""},
{"n": 6, "label": "implied", "why": "Accepting up to 5000 items needs a bounded body limit and per-item validation, or the import could exhaust memory or store invalid data; the 400 on an invalid item is requested."},
{"n": 7, "label": "requested", "why": "\"Each imported ticket is recorded and its requester is notified just as when one ticket is created\""},
{"n": 8, "label": "requested", "why": "\"Everything the service already does keeps working\""},
{"n": 9, "label": "requested", "why": "\"An import of 5000 tickets must be answered within 10 seconds\""}
]}
```
